summary.prose: Building s8 means one new git op-table builder, then eight small steps that each add a family of operations (or widen five existing tools) and prove their own coverage rows through executeTool in a temporary repository. The no-assigned-row rule is switched on only in the last Task, which also records the excluded commands, registers the tools, updates the inventory and snapshot tests, and runs the full sweep once.

tasks.title: Git op table: the family builder and the extension of an existing tool
tasks.summary: Add src/daemon/tools/builtins/git/op-table.ts with GitOpSpec, buildGitFamilyTool and extendGitTool: flat input schema with an op enum built from the gh field helpers, output union with a literal op, rules that refuse fields an op does not take, ref and path checks, stdin delivery through runShellBytes, cut-output and union checks, the per-op approval class (fixed or a function of the input), time limits and typed failures. No tool uses it yet. Unit tests with a stand-in git.
acceptanceChecks: buildGitFamilyTool throws at build time for a duplicate op, an op without a class, a stdin op without a stdin field and two ops that disagree about a shared field
A field the op does not take and a value outside its pattern are refused before any approval request is built
A cut stdout is a rejected failure whose partial text is not returned, and a result outside the op's answer member is a schema-mismatch failure with the original text kept
A stdin delivery error is a failure and no answer is parsed
extendGitTool keeps every existing input valid with the same result and class, and throws for a name or field collision
The gh files are unchanged

tasks.title: git_inspect: the read-only queries
tasks.summary: Add git_inspect (class none) with the read-only ops of the LLD (describe, name-rev, cherry, shortlog, show-branch, grep, last-modified, count-objects, var, version, check-attr, check-ignore, check-mailmap, check-ref-format, get-tar-commit-id, diff-files, diff-index, diff-pairs, range-diff, show-index, verify-commit, verify-tag, verify-pack, fsck, fsck-objects, pack-redundant, repo), each with its answer shape; a no-match exit gives a found false or an empty list. Mark each covered in the coverage table with a case through executeTool in a temporary repository. The no-assigned-row rule stays off until t9; this Task checks only its own rows.
acceptanceChecks: Every git_inspect op has a coverage case that runs through executeTool in a temporary repository and checks the result
A command that exits 1 to mean no match gives an empty answer, not a failure
No git_inspect op asks for approval
The coverage rows of these ops are covered, not assigned

tasks.title: Extend git_stash, git_worktree, git_remote, git_branch and git_tag
tasks.summary: Use extendGitTool to add the missing ops: stash (branch, create, store, export, import), worktree (lock, unlock, repair), remote (show, prune, update, set-head, set-branches, set-url --add, set-url --delete), branch (rename, copy, set-upstream-to, unset-upstream, edit-description) and tag (verify, sign). Remote prune is destructive. Re-pin the input snapshots with the new inputs listed as added by s8, and mark the rows covered with cases; only this Task's own rows are checked.
acceptanceChecks: Every input that was valid for the five tools gives the same result and class as before

tasks.title: Close out: exclusions, registration, inventory, docs and the full sweep
tasks.summary: Mark for-each-repo, hook, filter-branch, merge-octopus, merge-ours, merge-recursive, merge-recursive-ours, merge-recursive-theirs, merge-resolve, merge-subtree, subtree, request-pull and quiltimport excluded with the reasons the user gave (no program needs request-pull or quiltimport). Register the new tools in definitions.ts as withFailureNet(tool), update the inventory and registration tests, turn on the rule in git-coverage.test.ts that fails for any row still assigned, write the s8 outcome in docs/plans/tool-registry.md, then run the full sweep once.
acceptanceChecks: No coverage row is assigned; every excluded row has a reason; every command of GIT_2_53_COMMANDS has a row
Each of for-each-repo, hook, filter-branch, the seven merge strategy drivers, subtree, request-pull and quiltimport is an excluded row with a reason, and the rule fails when one is left assigned
The inventory test compares gitToolDefinitions with every tool the git files export
The full sweep matches the known baseline failures and adds none
docs/plans/tool-registry.md records the s8 outcome and the user's decisions

testStrategyCoverage.lldStrategyItem: buildGitFamilyTool makes a flat input schema with an op enum and an output union whose members carry the literal op, refuses a field the op does not take and a value outside its pattern before any approval request, and throws at build time for a duplicate op, an op without a class or a stdin op without a stdin field

the approval function of a family tool returns none for a read, common for an ordinary change and destructive for each operation the destructive rule lists, and for an input-dependent class (restore with worktree, checkout-index with force, gc with prune now, archive with an output path) returns destructive for the dangerous input and common for the safe one
a result that does not match the op's answer member is a schema-mismatch failure with the original text kept, and a cut stdout is a rejected failure whose partial text is not returned

extendGitTool keeps every input that is valid for git_stash, git_worktree, git_remote, git_branch and git_tag giving the same result and the same class, adds the new ops, and throws at build time for a name or field collision

git-coverage.test.ts has one case for every covered row of the s8 commands and operations (git_inspect, git_text, git_objects, git_patch, git_tree, git_maintenance, git_setup, git_refs, git_reflog and the new ops of git_stash, git_worktree, git_remote, git_branch and git_tag), each through executeTool against a temporary repository with the result and the effect (the object, ref, file or listing) checked, and fails for a covered row without a case, an excluded row without a reason, a command of GIT_2_53_COMMANDS without a row and any row still assigned

each operation that reads standard input (apply, am, mktree, mktag, fast-import, unpack-objects, index-pack, pack-objects, patch-id, stripspace, interpret-trailers, fmt-merge-msg, column, mailinfo, mailsplit, update-index and any other the table marks) receives the content given as its input and changes the repository as the command does, and a delivery that fails (git exits before reading) is a failure of the tool with no answer
each destructive operation asks for approval and is denied with no client attached before git starts, so the repository is unchanged, and an input the schema refuses never builds an approval request
a failed command gives the typed failure kind: missing-tool when git cannot start, timed-out with the unknown-outcome text for a changing operation, rejected with git's message otherwise

the inventory test (typed-git-tools.test.ts) compares gitToolDefinitions with every tool the git files export, the registration test registers each as withFailureNet(tool), and the pinned input snapshot (git-approval.test.ts) lists the new tools and inputs as added by s8 while every input of the 40 existing tools is unchanged
